title: Socket-level ACK-separation characterization
status_reason: Behavior reproduced from fresh loopback PCAPs: pure ACKs classified by packet fields, the app-write-delay transition measured with repeated samples (coarse 0-100 ms + refined 1 ms), the RQ3 socket-option factorial measured (TCP_NODELAY no effect; TCP_QUICKACK forces separation; response-size independent), environment recorded, no ACK forged, zero retransmissions/duplicate-ACKs/resets and 100% byte-identity reported. The one remaining open condition is the human packet-inspection worksheet (validation/phase03_human_packet_validation.csv), which an AI cannot complete.
test_summary: 56 passed (pytest tests/); byte-identity 875/875 matrix, 1400/1400 coarse, 600/600 refined

capture_environment.interface: lo (loopback), single host, no NIC offloads

measured_results.matrix_nonfirst_separate: 0/100 for all 7 configs (native, fixed25, bounded20-30, fixed300-rto105 bypass x full; crc-split adds 50 OTHER)

rq3_socket_options.tcp_nodelay_effect: none (nodelay on vs off identical: 0/80 at 25 ms, 80/80 at 50 ms)
rq3_socket_options.tcp_quickack_effect: forces separation (80/80 non-first at 25 ms vs baseline 0/80) -> user-space controllable
rq3_socket_options.response_size_effect: none (0% at 25 ms, 100% at 50 ms across 17-2407 B)
rq3_socket_options.not_varied: request size (all small READs) and kernel (single host)

supported_claims: On the tested host/kernel/socket config, a separate pure TCP ACK before the DNP3 response appears for non-first requests as the app-write delay crosses ~36-40 ms (100% at 40 ms); below ~35 ms responses stay COMBINED.
The transition is probabilistic (graded), not a sharp step; 50% near 39 ms.
Shipped normalization targets (fixed 25 ms, bounded 20-30 ms) keep the native COMBINED ACK mode with zero retransmissions/resets and 100% byte-identity.

RQ3 (this host/kernel): TCP_NODELAY has no effect on ACK separation; TCP_QUICKACK forces separation even at 25 ms (delayed-ACK effect controllable from user space); response size (17-2407 B) has no effect.
unsupported_claims: That Linux always uses a 40 ms delayed ACK (transition is graded and config-specific).
Any behavior on the Vision/Hulk rig, physical NICs, other kernels, or the real SEL-751/AB1400/ION7550 devices.
Kernel-dependence (single kernel measured) or request-size dependence (request size not varied).
That a separate ACK was independently synthesized or manipulated (Phase 04, not attempted).
open_blockers: Human packet-inspection worksheet not yet completed/signed (reviewer verdicts blank by design).
